1. Read what the kalimba is.

## What it is

- Metal **tines** on a board or box, plucked with the thumbs: a **lamellophone** (Wikipedia, "Mbira").
- The name and design are **Hugh Tracey**'s (late 1950s), modelled on the Zimbabwean **mbira nyunga nyunga**; it spread the instrument outside Africa (Wikipedia). It is not the mbira, and the mbira is much older.
- 17 tines here, in a major scale, **lowest in the centre**, going up **alternately left and right** (lowest-in-the-centre is common: Wikipedia; which side first: unverified).

## How it sounds

- A tine is a clamped bar: its overtones are at about **6.3** and **17.5** times the note, **inharmonic**; they are strongest at the attack and die fast, leaving an almost pure tone (Wikipedia, "Mbira").
- Neighbouring tines vibrate a little too (Wikipedia). Shorter tine: higher note (here the lengths are drawn from the pitch).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="wi-step" data-item="kalimba" data-set="{}" data-hit="tine:0"><p><b>The centre tine: the lowest.</b></p></div>
<div class="wi-step" data-item="kalimba" data-set="{}" data-hit="tine:1"><p><b>One to the left: the next note up.</b></p></div>
<div class="wi-step" data-item="kalimba" data-set="{}" data-hit="tine:2"><p><b>One to the right: the next.</b></p></div>
<div class="wi-step" data-item="kalimba" data-set="{&quot;buzz&quot;:true}" data-hit="tine:0"><p><b>With a buzzer.</b> (An mbira has them; this is a what-if.)</p></div>
<div class="wi-step" data-item="kalimba" data-set="{&quot;tuning&quot;:&quot;nyamaropa&quot;}" data-hit="tine:6"><p><b>Retuned to Nyamaropa.</b> The seventh note drops.</p></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Lamellophone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamellophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamellophone). Plucked tines; many African names (mbira, likembe, kalimba, sanza); marimbula.

"Mbira." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbira). Shona instrument of Zimbabwe; lamellophone; Hugh Tracey's kalimba (late 1950s) after the nyunga nyunga; inharmonic overtones strongest in the attack; adjacent tines vibrate; lowest notes in the centre is common; tunings not on the Western grid; Nyamaropa ~Mixolydian, Katsanzaira ~Dorian, Mavembe ~Phrygian; mbira dzavadzimu 22-28 keys, three registers (two left, one right); bottle-cap buzzers (machachara); deze calabash resonator; Nhema Musasa; UNESCO 2020.

**For students**

"Earth, Wind & Fire." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth,_Wind_%26_Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth,_Wind_%26_Fire). Known for its kalimba sound; "Kalimba Story"; Kalimba Productions.
